    "text": "MFS Payment Portal Design System. Design system for the Meridian Financial Services customer-facing payment portal (mfs-customer-portal). Last modified: 2026-09-28 by Wei Zhang. Owner: Payments Core squad (Arjun Deshmukh). Overview. This design system provides the foundational components, tokens, and patterns used across the MFS customer portal. It is implemented in the mfs-customer-portal repository using React and Tailwind CSS. The design system supports both light and dark themes and meets WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards. Components. PaymentForm: Primary payment entry form with card number input, expiry, CVV, and amount fields. Implements inline validation using the validateCard function. Supports real-time fraud score display from FraudAlertBanner. Variants: standard (single payment), recurring (subscription setup), quick-pay (saved card). States: idle, validating, processing, success, error, fraud-blocked. TransactionRow: Table row component for displaying individual transactions in the TransactionHistory page. Shows formatted amount (formatCurrency), date (formatDate), status badge, and action buttons. Supports click-to-expand for transaction details. CardDisplay: Visual card representation showing masked card number (maskCardNumber), card brand logo, and expiry date. Supports card flip animation for CVV display. Variants: physical card, virtual card, expired card. FraudAlertBanner: Alert banner displayed when a transaction receives a high fraud score. Shows risk level, suggested action, and dismiss button (dismissAlert). Severity variants: warning (medium risk), danger (high risk), critical (critical risk). Color Tokens. Primary: MFS Blue #1B4F72 (brand primary, used for CTAs and navigation). Secondary: MFS Teal #148F77 (secondary actions, success states). Danger: #C0392B (error states, fraud alerts, destructive actions). Warning: #F39C12 (medium risk alerts, pending states). Success: #27AE60 (completed payments, approved transactions). Neutral: Gray scale from #F8F9FA to #212529. Dark theme overrides: Primary #5DADE2, Background #1A1A2E, Surface #16213E. Typography. Font family: Inter (headings), Source Sans Pro (body). Scale: 12px (caption), 14px (body small), 16px (body), 20px (h4), 24px (h3), 32px (h2), 40px (h1). Font weight: 400 (regular), 500 (medium), 600 (semibold), 700 (bold). Layout Grid. Base grid: 8px. Content max-width: 1280px. Sidebar: 280px fixed. Main content area: fluid with 24px gutter. Responsive breakpoints: 320px (mobile), 768px (tablet), 1024px (desktop), 1440px (wide).",

    "text": "MFS Fraud Dashboard. Internal dashboard design for the Meridian Financial Services fraud and compliance team. Last modified: 2026-09-25 by Omar Hassan. Owner: Fraud and Risk squad (Priya Natarajan). Overview. The fraud dashboard provides real-time visibility into fraud scoring, AML alerts, and model performance for the mfs-fraud-engine. It is used by the Fraud and Risk squad and the compliance team for daily operations. Data sources: mfs_fraud_db on pghost-prod-02.mfs.internal, fraud-scores and aml-alerts Kafka topics, MLflow registry at mlflow.mfs.internal. Dashboard Layout. Top bar: Global filters (date range, risk level, model version), real-time toggle, refresh interval. Left sidebar: Navigation (Overview, Fraud Scores, AML Alerts, Model Performance, Velocity Monitor, Reports). Main content: Responsive grid with draggable panels. The dashboard renders data from the mfs-fraud-engine via the Fraud Scoring API v2 at api-gateway.mfs.internal/fraud/v2. Key Visualizations. Real-Time Score Distribution: Histogram of fraud scores in the last hour, binned by risk level (low 0-0.3, medium 0.3-0.6, high 0.6-0.85, critical 0.85-1.0). Data from fraud_scores table. Transaction Velocity Heat Map: Heat map showing transaction velocity by hour-of-day and day-of-week. Color intensity represents deviation from baseline. Data from velocity_windows in redis-cluster.mfs.internal. Geographic Risk Map: World map with color-coded transaction origins. Highlights high-risk jurisdictions flagged by FeatureExtractor.extract_geo_risk. Fraud Score Trend: Time series showing average ml_score, rule_score, and final_score over the selected period. Includes model version annotations. AML Alert Funnel: Funnel chart showing alert flow: total -> open -> under_review -> cleared / escalated. Data from aml_alerts table. Alert Management Panel. Table of active AML alerts from mfs_fraud_db.aml_alerts. Columns: alert_id, txn_id, customer_id, rule_id (STRUCT-001, RAPID-001, GEO-001, MERCH-001), severity, status, created_at. Inline actions: Assign analyst, update status, add notes. Filter by status (open, under_review), severity, rule type, date range. Escalated alerts trigger SAR filing workflow. Model Performance View. Current production model: fraud-xgb-v4.2 (F1=0.9612, Precision=0.9734, Recall=0.9493, AUC-ROC=0.9891). Canary model: fraud-xgb-v4.3 (F1=0.9654, 5% traffic). Performance metrics: Confusion matrix, ROC curve, precision-recall curve. A/B comparison between production and canary model predictions. Weekly retraining metrics trend. Data from models table in mfs_fraud_db and MLflow at mlflow.mfs.internal:5000.",

    "text": "MFS Customer Portal Redesign. Complete redesign of the Meridian Financial Services customer portal (mfs-customer-portal). Project initiated: 2026-08-01. Target completion: 2026-11-15. Last modified: 2026-09-30 by Lisa Park. Design lead: Wei Zhang. Product owner: Samantha Rodriguez (Director of Engineering). Overview. The portal redesign aims to modernize the customer-facing payment experience, improve transaction visibility, and integrate real-time fraud protection feedback. The redesign will be implemented in the mfs-customer-portal repository (TypeScript/React). Key goals: Reduce payment completion time by 30%, improve transaction search and filtering, surface fraud protection status to customers, full mobile-first responsive design, WCAG 2.1 AA compliance. User Flows. Payment Flow: Dashboard -> PaymentForm -> Card validation (validateCard) -> Fraud check (checkFraudScore via fraudApi) -> Payment processing (createPayment via paymentApi) -> Confirmation. If fraud score is high, FraudAlertBanner is shown with additional verification step. Transaction Review Flow: Dashboard -> TransactionHistory (fetchTransactions) -> TransactionRow (expand) -> Transaction detail with timeline -> Dispute / Refund action. Card Management Flow: Dashboard -> CardDisplay (list cards) -> Add new card (tokenize via Token Vault) -> Set default card -> Remove card. Page Designs. Dashboard (src/pages/Dashboard.tsx): Summary cards showing account balance, recent transactions, pending payments, and fraud alerts. Quick-pay widget using PaymentForm (quick-pay variant). Recent activity feed showing last 5 transactions using TransactionRow component. Links to usePayment and useTransactions hooks. Transaction History (src/pages/TransactionHistory.tsx): Full transaction listing with search, date range filter, status filter, and amount range filter. Uses useTransactions hook with infinite scroll pagination. Each row uses TransactionRow component with expand-on-click for full details. Export to CSV functionality. Payment Page: Full PaymentForm component with saved card selector (CardDisplay). Amount entry with formatCurrency preview. Fraud score feedback via FraudAlertBanner integrated directly below the form. Mobile Responsive Design. Mobile-first approach using Tailwind CSS responsive utilities. Breakpoints: 320px (small phone), 375px (phone), 768px (tablet), 1024px (desktop). Payment form stacks vertically on mobile with full-width inputs. Transaction history uses card layout on mobile, table layout on desktop. Bottom navigation on mobile replaces sidebar. Accessibility. Color contrast ratios meet WCAG 2.1 AA (minimum 4.5:1 for text). All interactive elements are keyboard navigable. ARIA labels on all form inputs and buttons. Screen reader support for FraudAlertBanner severity announcements. Focus management on modal dialogs and page transitions.",

    ]

    "text": "MFS Design System - Component Library. Core UI component library for all Meridian Financial Services applications. Last modified: 2026-09-30 by Wei Zhang. Owner: Payments Core squad (Arjun Deshmukh). Design system version: 3.2. Overview. The MFS Design System provides a unified set of reusable UI components, design tokens, and patterns used across the MFS customer portal, fraud dashboard, and internal tools. Built with React and Tailwind CSS. Storybook documentation at storybook.mfs.internal. All components support light and dark themes and meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards. Button Components. Button: Primary interactive element. Variants: primary (MFS Blue, main CTAs), secondary (outlined, secondary actions), danger (red, destructive actions like delete or cancel payment), ghost (text-only, tertiary actions). Sizes: small (32px height), medium (40px height), large (48px height). States: default, hover, active, focused, disabled, loading (with spinner). All buttons include focus ring for keyboard navigation and aria-label for screen readers. Input Components. Input: Text input field. Types: text (default), number (with increment/decrement), password (with show/hide toggle), search (with clear button and search icon). States: default, focused, filled, error (with error message below), disabled. Includes optional label, helper text, and character counter. Select: Dropdown selector with search-as-you-type filtering. Supports single and multi-select. DatePicker: Calendar-based date selection. Supports single date, date range, and relative date presets (today, last 7 days, last 30 days, custom range). Data Display Components. Table: Data table with built-in sorting (click column header), filtering (column-level filters), and pagination (configurable page sizes: 10, 25, 50, 100). Supports row selection, expandable rows, and sticky headers. Responsive: collapses to card layout on mobile. Badge: Status indicator. Variants: status (success/warning/error/info with colored dot), severity (CRITICAL red, HIGH orange, MEDIUM yellow, LOW gray). Card: Content container with optional header, body, footer, and action buttons. Supports elevated and flat variants. Feedback Components. Modal: Overlay dialog for confirmations, forms, and detail views. Sizes: small (400px), medium (600px), large (800px). Includes focus trap and escape-to-close. Toast: Temporary notification banner. Variants: success (green), error (red), warning (amber), info (blue). Auto-dismiss after configurable duration (default 5 seconds). Stacks up to 3 toasts vertically. Navigation Components. Avatar: User avatar with initials fallback. Sizes: 24px, 32px, 40px, 56px. Breadcrumb: Navigation trail showing current page location. Tabs: Horizontal tab navigation with lazy-loaded content panels. Supports icons and badge counts on tab labels. Accordion: Collapsible content sections. Supports single-open and multi-open modes. Color Tokens. All colors are defined as design tokens for consistent theming. primary-blue: #1A73E8 (brand primary, CTAs, navigation active state, links). success-green: #34A853 (success states, approved transactions, verified status). danger-red: #EA4335 (error states, fraud alerts, declined transactions, destructive actions). warning-amber: #FBBC04 (warning states, medium risk alerts, pending status). neutral-50: #F8F9FA (light background). neutral-900: #212529 (dark text). Dark theme overrides: primary-blue-dark #8AB4F8, background-dark #1A1A2E, surface-dark #16213E, text-dark #E8EAED. Typography Scale. Font family: Inter (all text). Font sizes: 12px (caption, meta text), 14px (body small, table cells), 16px (body default, form inputs), 20px (h4, section headings), 24px (h3, card titles), 32px (h2, page section headings). Font weights: 400 regular (body text), 500 medium (labels, navigation), 600 semibold (subheadings), 700 bold (headings, emphasis). Line heights: 1.4 (body), 1.2 (headings).",

    "text": "Fraud Investigation Dashboard - Interactive Prototype. Interactive prototype for the fraud investigation workflow used by the Fraud and Risk squad and compliance analysts. Last modified: 2026-09-28 by Omar Hassan. Owner: Fraud and Risk squad (Priya Natarajan). Product owner: Samantha Rodriguez (Director of Engineering). Overview. The fraud investigation dashboard provides analysts with a unified interface for reviewing fraud cases, examining transaction evidence, and recording investigation dispositions. Data sources: mfs_fraud_db on pghost-prod-02.mfs.internal via the Case Management API and Fraud Scoring API. The dashboard is implemented as part of the mfs-fraud-dashboard application (React/TypeScript). Dashboard Layout. Three-panel layout optimized for investigator workflows. Left sidebar (320px fixed width): case queue with filters. Main panel (fluid width): case detail with transaction timeline and evidence. Right panel (280px fixed width, collapsible): analyst actions and disposition form. Top bar: global search, notification bell (new CRITICAL cases), analyst avatar with role indicator. Left Sidebar - Case Queue. Case list displaying all assigned and unassigned cases. Each case card shows: case_id, priority badge (CRITICAL red, HIGH orange, MEDIUM yellow, LOW gray), status badge, title (truncated), customer_id, created_at relative time. Filter controls: priority multi-select (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW), status multi-select (NEW, ASSIGNED, IN_REVIEW, DISPOSITION, CLOSED), date range picker, assigned analyst dropdown. Sort options: priority (default), newest first, oldest first. Real-time updates via WebSocket when new cases are created or statuses change. Unassigned CRITICAL cases pulse with red border animation. Main Panel - Case Detail. Transaction timeline: vertical timeline showing all transactions linked to the case, each with timestamp, amount (formatted via formatCurrency), status, and fraud score. Click a transaction to expand full detail card. Evidence cards: grid layout showing collected evidence from multiple sources (transaction records, fraud scores, AML alerts, customer records). Each card shows source_type icon, summary, and relevance score. Click to expand full evidence detail in modal. Risk score gauge: circular gauge visualization showing the composite fraud score (0.0-1.0) with color gradient from green (low) to red (critical). Gauge includes model version label and confidence interval. Geographic map: interactive map showing transaction origin locations plotted by IP geolocation. Color-coded markers: green (normal), yellow (elevated risk), red (high-risk jurisdiction). Supports zoom, pan, and click-for-details on each marker. Customer profile sidebar: compact view showing customer name (masked), kyc_status, risk_level, account age, and transaction history summary. Right Panel - Analyst Actions. Assign button: assign case to self or select analyst from dropdown. Changes status to ASSIGNED. Escalate button: escalate to supervisor with required justification text. Triggers PagerDuty alert for CRITICAL escalations. Disposition form: decision select (confirmed_fraud, false_positive, suspicious_activity, insufficient_evidence), rationale text area (required, minimum 50 characters), recommended actions checklist, SAR required toggle. Submit creates disposition record and transitions case to DISPOSITION status. Notes section: chronological list of analyst notes with add-note text area. Interactive States. Case selection: clicking a case in the left sidebar loads its full detail in the main panel with smooth transition animation. Evidence drill-down: clicking an evidence card opens a modal with full evidence detail, source links, and related records. Disposition form: form validation requires all mandatory fields. Submit shows confirmation dialog before recording decision. Toast notification confirms successful disposition. Responsive Breakpoints. Desktop (1440px and above): full three-panel layout as described. Tablet (768px to 1439px): left sidebar collapses to icon-only mode, right panel becomes a slide-out drawer triggered by action button. Case queue and case detail share the main viewport with tab navigation. Mobile (below 768px): single-panel layout with bottom navigation tabs for case queue, case detail, and actions. Optimized for read-only case review on mobile; disposition actions require desktop or tablet.",

    "headings": [
      "Mobile Payment Flow Prototype",
      "Overview",
      "User Journey Steps",
      "Step 1: Merchant Selection",
      "Step 2: Amount Entry",
      "Step 3: Payment Method Selection",
      "Step 4: Review & Confirm",

    "text": "Mobile Payment Flow - User Journey. Interactive prototype for the mobile payment experience on the MFS customer portal. Last modified: 2026-09-30 by Lisa Park. Design lead: Wei Zhang. Owner: Payments Core squad (Arjun Deshmukh). Overview. This prototype defines the complete mobile payment user journey from merchant selection through payment confirmation. Designed mobile-first for the mfs-customer-portal responsive experience. Integrates with Payment Gateway API v2 and Fraud Scoring API v2. Target: reduce payment completion time by 30% compared to current flow. User Journey Steps. The payment flow consists of 6 sequential screens with clear progress indication via a step indicator bar at the top. Step 1: Merchant Selection. Search or browse merchants from a categorized list. Recent merchants section shows last 5 merchants for quick access. Each merchant card displays: merchant name, category, logo, and verification badge. Selecting a merchant advances to Step 2 with a slide-left transition. Step 2: Amount Entry. Large numeric keypad optimized for thumb reach on mobile. Amount displayed in large font (32px) with real-time currency formatting via formatCurrency. Currency selector (default USD) with support for EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, JPY. Optional memo/description field. Amount validation: minimum $0.01, maximum per-merchant limit. Step 3: Payment Method Selection. List of saved payment methods using CardDisplay component. Each card shows: card brand logo, masked card number (last 4 digits via maskCardNumber), expiry date, default indicator. Options: select a saved card, add new card (opens tokenization flow via Token Vault API), or bank transfer (ACH). New card entry: card number, expiry, CVV fields with inline validation using validateCard function. Card is tokenized immediately via POST /tokens/v1/tokenize before proceeding. Step 4: Review & Confirm. Summary screen showing: merchant name, payment amount (formatted), selected payment method (masked card), and memo. Edit links for each field to return to the relevant step. Terms and conditions checkbox. Confirm Payment button (primary, full-width) with biometric authentication option (FaceID/TouchID). Step 5: Processing Animation. Full-screen processing state with animated progress indicator. Three phases visualized: (1) Securing payment (tokenization check), (2) Fraud check (real-time fraud scoring via Fraud Scoring API, fraud_score displayed as a shield icon with checkmark for low risk), (3) Processing payment (payment creation via Payment Gateway API). Each phase shows a checkmark animation on completion. If fraud check returns high risk (fraud_score > 0.60), FraudAlertBanner appears with additional verification step before proceeding. Step 6: Result Screen. Success state: green checkmark animation, transaction ID, amount, merchant name, timestamp, and a Share Receipt button. Includes Add to Favorites option for the merchant. Failure state: red X animation with clear error message and recommended action. Includes Retry Payment and Contact Support buttons. Transaction details are saved and accessible from TransactionHistory. Error States. Network timeout: shown after 30 seconds of no response. Message: 'Connection timed out. Please check your internet connection and try again.' Retry button available. Card declined: shown when payment processor returns decline. Message: 'Your card was declined. Please try a different payment method or contact your bank.' Suggests selecting a different saved card. Fraud hold: shown when fraud_score exceeds critical threshold (> 0.85). Message: 'This transaction requires additional verification for your security.' Presents identity verification step (selfie or OTP). FraudAlertBanner displayed with severity: critical. Insufficient funds: shown for bank transfer payments. Message: 'Insufficient funds in the selected account.' Suggests selecting a different payment method. Accessibility. Full WCAG 2.1 AA compliance verified. VoiceOver (iOS) tested: all screens, buttons, and form inputs have descriptive aria-labels. Dynamic announcements for processing phase transitions and result state. TalkBack (Android) tested: equivalent screen reader support with focus management. Color contrast: all text meets minimum 4.5:1 ratio against backgrounds in both light and dark themes. Touch targets: minimum 44x44px for all interactive elements. Reduced motion: processing animation respects prefers-reduced-motion setting, replacing animation with static progress indicators. Font scaling: supports dynamic type up to 200% without layout breakage.",

      "https://figma.mfs.internal/files/MFS-PAY-PORTAL-2026",

    ]
  }
]

Last modified: 2026-09-30 by Lisa Park. Design lead: Wei Zhang. Product owner: Samantha Rodriguez (Director of Engineering). Overview. The portal redesign aims to modernize the customer-facing payment experience, improve transaction visibility, and integrate real-time fraud protection feedback. The redesign will be implemented in the mfs-customer-portal repository (TypeScript/React). Key goals: Reduce payment completion time by 30%, improve transaction search and filtering, surface fraud protection status to customers, full mobile-first responsive design, WCAG 2.1 AA compliance. User Flows. Payment Flow: Dashboard -> PaymentForm -> Card validation (validateCard) -> Fraud check (checkFraudScore via fraudApi) -> Payment processing (createPayment via paymentApi) -> Confirmation. If fraud score is high, FraudAlertBanner is shown with additional verification step. Transaction Review Flow: Dashboard -> TransactionHistory (fetchTransactions) -> TransactionRow (expand) -> Transaction detail with timeline -> Dispute / Refund action. Card Management Flow: Dashboard -> CardDisplay (list cards) -> Add new card (tokenize via Token Vault) -> Set default card -> Remove card. Page Designs. Dashboard (src/pages/Dashboard.tsx): Summary cards showing account balance, recent transactions, pending payments, and fraud alerts. Quick-pay widget using PaymentForm (quick-pay variant). Recent activity feed showing last 5 transactions using TransactionRow component. Links to usePayment and useTransactions hooks. Transaction History (src/pages/TransactionHistory.tsx): Full transaction listing with search, date range filter, status filter, and amount range filter. Uses useTransactions hook with infinite scroll pagination. Each row uses TransactionRow component with expand-on-click for full details. Export to CSV functionality. Payment Page: Full PaymentForm component with saved card selector (CardDisplay). Amount entry with formatCurrency preview. Fraud score feedback via FraudAlertBanner integrated directly below the form. Mobile Responsive Design. Mobile-first approach using Tailwind CSS responsive utilities. Breakpoints: 320px (small phone), 375px (phone), 768px (tablet), 1024px (desktop). Payment form stacks vertically on mobile with full-width inputs. Transaction history uses card layout on mobile, table layout on desktop. Bottom navigation on mobile replaces sidebar. Accessibility. Color contrast ratios meet WCAG 2.1 AA (minimum 4.5:1 for text). All interactive elements are keyboard navigable. ARIA labels on all form inputs and buttons. Screen reader support for FraudAlertBanner severity announcements. Focus management on modal dialogs and page transitions.

data.title: MFS Design System - Component Library
data.text: MFS Design System - Component Library. Core UI component library for all Meridian Financial Services applications. Last modified: 2026-09-30 by Wei Zhang. Owner: Payments Core squad (Arjun Deshmukh). Design system version: 3.2. Overview. The MFS Design System provides a unified set of reusable UI components, design tokens, and patterns used across the MFS customer portal, fraud dashboard, and internal tools. Built with React and Tailwind CSS. Storybook documentation at storybook.mfs.internal. All components support light and dark themes and meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards. Button Components. Button: Primary interactive element. Variants: primary (MFS Blue, main CTAs), secondary (outlined, secondary actions), danger (red, destructive actions like delete or cancel payment), ghost (text-only, tertiary actions). Sizes: small (32px height), medium (40px height), large (48px height). States: default, hover, active, focused, disabled, loading (with spinner). All buttons include focus ring for keyboard navigation and aria-label for screen readers. Input Components. Input: Text input field. Types: text (default), number (with increment/decrement), password (with show/hide toggle), search (with clear button and search icon). States: default, focused, filled, error (with error message below), disabled. Includes optional label, helper text, and character counter. Select: Dropdown selector with search-as-you-type filtering. Supports single and multi-select. DatePicker: Calendar-based date selection. Supports single date, date range, and relative date presets (today, last 7 days, last 30 days, custom range). Data Display Components. Table: Data table with built-in sorting (click column header), filtering (column-level filters), and pagination (configurable page sizes: 10, 25, 50, 100). Supports row selection, expandable rows, and sticky headers. Responsive: collapses to card layout on mobile. Badge: Status indicator. Variants: status (success/warning/error/info with colored dot), severity (CRITICAL red, HIGH orange, MEDIUM yellow, LOW gray). Card: Content container with optional header, body, footer, and action buttons. Supports elevated and flat variants. Feedback Components. Modal: Overlay dialog for confirmations, forms, and detail views. Sizes: small (400px), medium (600px), large (800px). Includes focus trap and escape-to-close. Toast: Temporary notification banner. Variants: success (green), error (red), warning (amber), info (blue). Auto-dismiss after configurable duration (default 5 seconds). Stacks up to 3 toasts vertically. Navigation Components. Avatar: User avatar with initials fallback. Sizes: 24px, 32px, 40px, 56px. Breadcrumb: Navigation trail showing current page location. Tabs: Horizontal tab navigation with lazy-loaded content panels. Supports icons and badge counts on tab labels. Accordion: Collapsible content sections. Supports single-open and multi-open modes. Color Tokens. All colors are defined as design tokens for consistent theming. primary-blue: #1A73E8 (brand primary, CTAs, navigation active state, links). success-green: #34A853 (success states, approved transactions, verified status). danger-red: #EA4335 (error states, fraud alerts, declined transactions, destructive actions). warning-amber: #FBBC04 (warning states, medium risk alerts, pending status). neutral-50: #F8F9FA (light background). neutral-900: #212529 (dark text). Dark theme overrides: primary-blue-dark #8AB4F8, background-dark #1A1A2E, surface-dark #16213E, text-dark #E8EAED. Typography Scale. Font family: Inter (all text). Font sizes: 12px (caption, meta text), 14px (body small, table cells), 16px (body default, form inputs), 20px (h4, section headings), 24px (h3, card titles), 32px (h2, page section headings). Font weights: 400 regular (body text), 500 medium (labels, navigation), 600 semibold (subheadings), 700 bold (headings, emphasis). Line heights: 1.4 (body), 1.2 (headings).

data.title: Fraud Investigation Dashboard - Interactive Prototype
data.text: Fraud Investigation Dashboard - Interactive Prototype. Interactive prototype for the fraud investigation workflow used by the Fraud and Risk squad and compliance analysts. Last modified: 2026-09-28 by Omar Hassan. Owner: Fraud and Risk squad (Priya Natarajan). Product owner: Samantha Rodriguez (Director of Engineering). Overview. The fraud investigation dashboard provides analysts with a unified interface for reviewing fraud cases, examining transaction evidence, and recording investigation dispositions. Data sources: mfs_fraud_db on pghost-prod-02.mfs.internal via the Case Management API and Fraud Scoring API. The dashboard is implemented as part of the mfs-fraud-dashboard application (React/TypeScript). Dashboard Layout. Three-panel layout optimized for investigator workflows. Left sidebar (320px fixed width): case queue with filters. Main panel (fluid width): case detail with transaction timeline and evidence. Right panel (280px fixed width, collapsible): analyst actions and disposition form. Top bar: global search, notification bell (new CRITICAL cases), analyst avatar with role indicator. Left Sidebar - Case Queue. Case list displaying all assigned and unassigned cases. Each case card shows: case_id, priority badge (CRITICAL red, HIGH orange, MEDIUM yellow, LOW gray), status badge, title (truncated), customer_id, created_at relative time. Filter controls: priority multi-select (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW), status multi-select (NEW, ASSIGNED, IN_REVIEW, DISPOSITION, CLOSED), date range picker, assigned analyst dropdown. Sort options: priority (default), newest first, oldest first. Real-time updates via WebSocket when new cases are created or statuses change. Unassigned CRITICAL cases pulse with red border animation. Main Panel - Case Detail. Transaction timeline: vertical timeline showing all transactions linked to the case, each with timestamp, amount (formatted via formatCurrency), status, and fraud score. Click a transaction to expand full detail card. Evidence cards: grid layout showing collected evidence from multiple sources (transaction records, fraud scores, AML alerts, customer records). Each card shows source_type icon, summary, and relevance score. Click to expand full evidence detail in modal. Risk score gauge: circular gauge visualization showing the composite fraud score (0.0-1.0) with color gradient from green (low) to red (critical). Gauge includes model version label and confidence interval. Geographic map: interactive map showing transaction origin locations plotted by IP geolocation. Color-coded markers: green (normal), yellow (elevated risk), red (high-risk jurisdiction). Supports zoom, pan, and click-for-details on each marker. Customer profile sidebar: compact view showing customer name (masked), kyc_status, risk_level, account age, and transaction history summary. Right Panel - Analyst Actions. Assign button: assign case to self or select analyst from dropdown. Changes status to ASSIGNED. Escalate button: escalate to supervisor with required justification text. Triggers PagerDuty alert for CRITICAL escalations. Disposition form: decision select (confirmed_fraud, false_positive, suspicious_activity, insufficient_evidence), rationale text area (required, minimum 50 characters), recommended actions checklist, SAR required toggle. Submit creates disposition record and transitions case to DISPOSITION status. Notes section: chronological list of analyst notes with add-note text area. Interactive States. Case selection: clicking a case in the left sidebar loads its full detail in the main panel with smooth transition animation. Evidence drill-down: clicking an evidence card opens a modal with full evidence detail, source links, and related records. Disposition form: form validation requires all mandatory fields. Submit shows confirmation dialog before recording decision. Toast notification confirms successful disposition. Responsive Breakpoints. Desktop (1440px and above): full three-panel layout as described. Tablet (768px to 1439px): left sidebar collapses to icon-only mode, right panel becomes a slide-out drawer triggered by action button. Case queue and case detail share the main viewport with tab navigation. Mobile (below 768px): single-panel layout with bottom navigation tabs for case queue, case detail, and actions. Optimized for read-only case review on mobile; disposition actions require desktop or tablet.

data.title: Mobile Payment Flow - User Journey
data.text: Mobile Payment Flow - User Journey. Interactive prototype for the mobile payment experience on the MFS customer portal. Last modified: 2026-09-30 by Lisa Park. Design lead: Wei Zhang. Owner: Payments Core squad (Arjun Deshmukh). Overview. This prototype defines the complete mobile payment user journey from merchant selection through payment confirmation. Designed mobile-first for the mfs-customer-portal responsive experience. Integrates with Payment Gateway API v2 and Fraud Scoring API v2. Target: reduce payment completion time by 30% compared to current flow. User Journey Steps. The payment flow consists of 6 sequential screens with clear progress indication via a step indicator bar at the top. Step 1: Merchant Selection. Search or browse merchants from a categorized list. Recent merchants section shows last 5 merchants for quick access. Each merchant card displays: merchant name, category, logo, and verification badge. Selecting a merchant advances to Step 2 with a slide-left transition. Step 2: Amount Entry. Large numeric keypad optimized for thumb reach on mobile. Amount displayed in large font (32px) with real-time currency formatting via formatCurrency. Currency selector (default USD) with support for EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, JPY. Optional memo/description field. Amount validation: minimum $0.01, maximum per-merchant limit. Step 3: Payment Method Selection. List of saved payment methods using CardDisplay component. Each card shows: card brand logo, masked card number (last 4 digits via maskCardNumber), expiry date, default indicator. Options: select a saved card, add new card (opens tokenization flow via Token Vault API), or bank transfer (ACH). New card entry: card number, expiry, CVV fields with inline validation using validateCard function. Card is tokenized immediately via POST /tokens/v1/tokenize before proceeding. Step 4: Review & Confirm. Summary screen showing: merchant name, payment amount (formatted), selected payment method (masked card), and memo. Edit links for each field to return to the relevant step. Terms and conditions checkbox. Confirm Payment button (primary, full-width) with biometric authentication option (FaceID/TouchID). Step 5: Processing Animation. Full-screen processing state with animated progress indicator. Three phases visualized: (1) Securing payment (tokenization check), (2) Fraud check (real-time fraud scoring via Fraud Scoring API, fraud_score displayed as a shield icon with checkmark for low risk), (3) Processing payment (payment creation via Payment Gateway API). Each phase shows a checkmark animation on completion. If fraud check returns high risk (fraud_score > 0.60), FraudAlertBanner appears with additional verification step before proceeding. Step 6: Result Screen. Success state: green checkmark animation, transaction ID, amount, merchant name, timestamp, and a Share Receipt button. Includes Add to Favorites option for the merchant. Failure state: red X animation with clear error message and recommended action. Includes Retry Payment and Contact Support buttons. Transaction details are saved and accessible from TransactionHistory. Error States. Network timeout: shown after 30 seconds of no response. Message: 'Connection timed out. Please check your internet connection and try again.' Retry button available. Card declined: shown when payment processor returns decline. Message: 'Your card was declined. Please try a different payment method or contact your bank.' Suggests selecting a different saved card. Fraud hold: shown when fraud_score exceeds critical threshold (> 0.85). Message: 'This transaction requires additional verification for your security.' Presents identity verification step (selfie or OTP). FraudAlertBanner displayed with severity: critical. Insufficient funds: shown for bank transfer payments. Message: 'Insufficient funds in the selected account.' Suggests selecting a different payment method. Accessibility. Full WCAG 2.1 AA compliance verified. VoiceOver (iOS) tested: all screens, buttons, and form inputs have descriptive aria-labels. Dynamic announcements for processing phase transitions and result state. TalkBack (Android) tested: equivalent screen reader support with focus management. Color contrast: all text meets minimum 4.5:1 ratio against backgrounds in both light and dark themes. Touch targets: minimum 44x44px for all interactive elements. Reduced motion: processing animation respects prefers-reduced-motion setting, replacing animation with static progress indicators. Font scaling: supports dynamic type up to 200% without layout breakage.
